gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a radar-wake parking setup costs $269 today: DDPAI sells its N5 Dual 2026 with the radar module and the OBD/hardwire kit for $269.00 (store.ddpai.com, read 2026-11-21). Thinkware's cheapest built-in-radar camera, the U3000 Front & Rear, is $479.99 and the U3000 PRO is $549.99 on thinkwarestore.com the same day. ChatGPT's third pick, the U1000 Plus, shows 'Out of Stock' and does not list a price for its radar module.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited. Thinkware's help-center article 'RADAR Parking Mode' lists only the U3000 PRO and U3000. Thinkware's Parking Mode page lists Thinkware models only and gives no price for the radar module. The Thinkware U3000 PRO product and global pages cover that one model. Digital Camera World's U3000 Pro review names only the Nextbase iQ as a rival, and the Nextbase iQ has no radar. I could not load the body of Tom's Guide's U3000 Pro review. None of these pages names a radar parking camera from any maker other than Thinkware, and none prices a radar setup under $479.99. The uncited results I saw (DCW's front-and-rear guide, dashboardcamerareviews, dashcamtalk) were not checked for DDPAI coverage. Only their titles were seen.
decides: The overall pick stays the Thinkware U3000 PRO Front & Rear. Its front and rear radar is built in, detection range adjusts from 1 to 5 m, an OBD-II cable comes in the box, and it has STARVIS 2 sensors front and rear. Its losses are price ($549.99) and Digital Camera World's finding that the default radar sensitivity is too high (rain set it off). DDPAI honestly takes the budget-radar segment. The N5 Dual 2026 radar bundle is the only radar-wake 4K setup I priced under $300 today. Our linked DDPAI N5 Pro takes the same radar accessory, which the store titles 'Radar Accessory for N5 Pro / N5 Dual' and lists at $80.00. The N5 Pro also has a 2K rear camera, against the N5 Dual's 1080p rear. That keeps a DDPAI product in the top three on the question's own terms, so no skip. The DDPAI segment has two weaknesses. The radar range in the AU retailer's spec is 3 m forward and 4 m rear, against Thinkware's 5 m maximum. And a named DashCamTalk owner reported OBD-kit power problems, for which DDPAI's reply recommended fuse-box wiring. The page should present DDPAI as the budget radar pick, not the overall winner.

findings.label: Owner-reported parking power problem (named)
findings.value: DashCamTalk user 'thatbwnguy' (2024-12-04) reported this setup in a 2019 Mazda CX-9. With the OBD hardwire kit, the camera recorded about 15 min after shut-off and then powered off, so the radar stopped working; the radar often went undetected. DDPAI's forum account 'linuxliu' replied (2025-08-18) that the OBD port may not report ACC status and recommended wiring to the fuse box.
findings.source_title: [DDPAI N5 Dual] Dashcam shutting down instead of sleeping + other power problems – DashCamTalk
findings.note: Single owner report, no measured current. Relevant to the page's install advice: use the fuse-box kit.
